findings.text: §4's done-when makes only "its moved tests" pass at the new location, but four tests that stay in `tests/` import the three modules through their `reckon.crew` path: `tests/test_a_lift_reaches_every_budget_row.py:31` (`pace_replay`), `tests/test_ledger_files_and_index_agree.py:12` (`carryover_census`, `death_census`), `tests/test_writer_callers_first_wave.py:283` (`carryover…`) and `tests/test_timestamp_callers_batch_a.py:36` (`pace_replay`); `scripts/` is not a package (no `__init__.py`), so those imports break on the move and the done-when stays green while the suite does not.

findings.reason: the cited model does not exhibit the parser that makes `--help` a real check, so a node mirroring `death_census.py` satisfies the measure with a script that mishandles the flag and fires an unwanted write during the gate; the done-when must require an actual parser when it asks the flag to exit 0.
findings.text: §4 says `carryover_census.py` and `pace_replay.py` "each gain a `main()` with an argument parser … as `death_census.py` already has", but `death_census.py` carries no argument parser: `main(argv)` (line 342) treats `argv[0]` as an output path and never parses a flag, so the done-when's "runs from `scripts/census/` with `--help` exiting 0" passes for the model only by ignoring `--help`, running a full census, and writing a file literally named `--help` before returning 0.
